sections.h2: Who bills a Las Vegas house?
sections.html:
The answer is Clark County. Las Vegas serves as the county seat, yet the assessing and billing are done by county offices: the Assessor sets value and the Treasurer sends the bill. The city counted 641,903 residents in 2020, and the metro area is estimated at 2.4 million.

A Las Vegas mailing label does not guarantee a city address. Paradise, Spring Valley, Enterprise and Summerlin South are unincorporated, while Henderson, North Las Vegas and Boulder City are separate cities. All of them pay property tax through the same Clark County offices, so everything below holds for each of them.

Visit or write the Treasurer at 500 S Grand Central Pkwy, Las Vegas, NV 89155-1220, or call (702) 455-4323. The counter is staffed Monday to Thursday, 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., with no service Friday through Sunday. To change where your bill is mailed, send the County Assessor the county's form.

One bill covers each fiscal year, which starts July 1 and ends June 30, and it can be paid in four parts. Dates: the third Monday of August, plus the first Monday of October, of January and of March. A yearly total of $100 or less cannot be split: all of it comes due with the first installment.

Only one bill is mailed per fiscal year. When nothing has arrived by August 1, the automated phone system will send a copy to the address on record. A 10-day grace period applies, and the payment has to arrive, or be postmarked, within 10 calendar days after the due date.

Mail handling is picky. A regular stamp with a postmark counts as on time. Metered mail, pre-canceled stamps, Automated Postal Center stamps and permit imprints carry no postmark, so an envelope that arrives late with one of those is treated as late.

After the grace period, penalties stack up:

  • One unpaid installment: 4%
  • Two unpaid: 5% added
  • Three unpaid: 6% added
  • All four late: 7%

Payment methodCost and notes
Online or phone, e-checkNo fee. Phone line is (702) 455-4323, option 1.
Online or phone, cardVisa, MasterCard or Discover, with a service fee charged by a third-party provider.
In personFirst floor of the County Government Center, behind security. Cash, check and debit cards, no fee.
Drop boxSouthwest side of the building, checks only.
MailCheck payable to the Clark County Treasurer, with parcel numbers and payment coupons.
Bank bill payAccepted, like the methods above.

If reminders would help, the county sends them by email or text ahead of each installment. Keep the confirmation after every payment. Should a mailed check go astray or a postmark be disputed, that record is what settles it.

sections.h2: What happens if the tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
If a balance is still open when April ends, the parcel is advertised as delinquent in the local newspaper and on the Treasurer's site. After three consecutive fiscal years of delinquency, the property is deeded to the Clark County Treasurer as trustee, under NRS 361.585 and 361.590. A property found abandoned for two consecutive fiscal years can follow the same path. Once deeded, it can be auctioned.

What the county says about its auctions:

  • Expect one auction a year at minimum, normally in spring, and occasionally a second in fall.
  • Buyers take the property as-is, every sale is final, and buyers get no redemption period.
  • The former owner has two years to protest the sale.
  • The opening bid must cover the taxes, penalties, interest and costs, and may also include sanitation, sewer, special improvement district and nuisance abatement charges.
  • Money bid above that minimum is excess proceeds, claimable within one year after the deed is recorded.

Paying before things get that far keeps the house in your hands. Special improvement district assessments run on their own track, with delinquency sales held four times a year.

Ask the Assessor's appraiser to look at the number again before anything formal. If the answer is still no, a petition for the Clark County Board of Equalization goes to the Assessor by January 15 (the next business day when that date falls on a weekend or holiday). Further review runs through the State Board of Equalization and finally District Court.

State law also slows how quickly a bill can rise. A single-family home you live in as your primary residence cannot see its tax rise more than 3% year over year, and everything else is held to a general abatement of up to 8%. Neither cap helps a parcel in its first year after new improvements or after a change in use. Assessed value is 35% of taxable value, and the combined rate is capped at $3.66 per $100 of assessed value.

Each tax district sets its own mix, which means a house in one corner of the valley can owe more than an identical house elsewhere. Rate tables by district and entity live on the Treasurer's site. Use the line for your parcel and ignore any citywide average you hear in conversation.

sections.h2: What transfer tax and recording cost
sections.html:
Transfer tax runs $2.55 for each $500 of value in this county, made up of the $1.95 state figure and a $0.60 county addition. It is paid to the County Recorder as the deed is recorded, with a Declaration of Value form attached to any document that conveys an interest in real property. Both parties to the sale are liable under the statute.

Some transfers escape the tax, such as moving a house into or out of a trust for no payment, or a deed upon death under NRS 111.109. Unsure about yours? Ask the Recorder, who reviews exemption applications.

sections.h2: What a closing looks like when tax is open
sections.html:
Here is the usual order. After an offer is accepted, the title company opens an order, obtains the current balance from the Treasurer, and shows it as a deduction on your side of the closing statement. Any installment already due is paid in full. The installment still running is usually divided between buyer and seller by days owned, which your title officer will calculate. If a special improvement district assessment is attached to the parcel, it shows up as its own line.

The worst surprises come from sellers who assume the lender handled everything. With an escrow account, the servicer pays on your behalf, but the county still treats you as the one responsible. Check your parcel's status yourself before you list.

sections.h2: Sorting out an inherited or rented property
sections.html: Two situations deserve extra care. If you inherited the house, the heirs take on the tax history along with the deed, so open installments and any delinquency notice need to be located early. A property that was rented out may no longer qualify for the 3% cap on a primary residence, which can make the next bill larger than the last one. Mention both facts to the title company so the numbers on the settlement statement match what the Treasurer and Assessor show.

Owing tax or a special assessment will not stop a closing. A payoff statement is requested by the title company and settled from your sale money. Cash Home Buyers purchases Las Vegas houses as-is, so there is no repair or listing prep before closing.

Paperwork helps. Have on hand your deed, newest tax bill, mortgage payoff letter if any, and a copy of any delinquency notice. Confirm every amount with the Clark County Treasurer and Recorder, since fees and dates reset each fiscal year.

faqs.q: Where do Las Vegas owners pay their property tax?
faqs.a: The Clark County Treasurer takes payment; the Assessor sets value on a separate track. Pay online, by phone at (702) 455-4323, by mail, or in person on Monday through Thursday.

faqs.q: When are Las Vegas property taxes due?
faqs.a: Four installments fall on the third Monday of August and the first Mondays of October, January and March, each followed by a 10-day grace period. A yearly total of $100 or less is due all at once, with installment one.

faqs.q: How much is the late penalty on Las Vegas property tax?
faqs.a: After the grace period, one unpaid installment draws 4%, with added penalties of 5%, 6% and 7% as two, three or all four go unpaid.

faqs.q: How long do I have to contest a Las Vegas assessment?
faqs.a: January 15 (or the next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). Send the petition to the Clark County Assessor, who forwards it to the County Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Can the county auction my Las Vegas house for unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Eventually, yes. Three straight fiscal years of delinquency lets the property be deeded to the County Treasurer as trustee and then sold. Paying up, or selling first, keeps that from happening.
